item.title: October Writers Workshop at Watchung Booksellers — Sun Oct 25, 6:00 PM — watchung booksellers the kids’ room
item.description: Watchung Booksellers hosts a writers’ workshop for creatives who are stuck in their process with therapist Amos Kamil on Sunday, October 25 afrom 6:00 – 8:00 p.m. Stuck isn’t a discipline problem. Most workshops on creative block treat it as a craft problem — outline more, write badly on purpose, lower the stakes. Useful, but it treats the symptom. As a therapist who works with writers and creative people, Amos Kamil goes one layer deeper: block is usually not a craft failure, it’s a psychological pattern doing its job (protecting against exposure, failure, an old judgment) and it responds to different tools than craft advice does. The workshop’s promise: leave having identified your specific sabotage pattern and practiced one concrete tool against it, live. In this introductory workshop, you’ll leave with: *A named pattern (your own version of the “quiet agent” derailing you) *One practiced tool you can use again unassisted *A one-line diagnosis of where your current project is stu

item.title: Documentary Film Screening: Becoming Benjamin Lay — Tue Oct 27, 6:30 PM — Dickson Hall 176
item.description:
Please join the English and History students and faculty from the course Radical New Jersey to watch this new, limited release documentary on Benjamin Lay, Quaker rebel, early abolitionist, and New Jersey’s most radical son. 6:30pm, Thursday, October 27 in Dickson Hall 176. More information: In 1738, the four-foot Benjamin Lay famously stabbed a bible full of fake blood at a Quaker meeting, decades before abolition became a cause. He lived in a cave in Burlington County, was expelled from every Quaker meeting he entered, but refused to stop. In this documentary, actor Mark Povinelli adapts his one person show “The Return of Benjamin Lay” for a performance before the Little People of America conference in Baltimore in 2024. Permission to screen this documentary comes courtesy of the playwright, historian, and producer Marcus Rediker. Everybody is welcome!
Hosted by: College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHSS)

item.description:

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.
During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.
The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.
